newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Royale Belge says share worth 10,000 Bfr.
newsitem.headline: Royale Belge says share worth 10,000 Bfr.

text.p: Belgian insurance company Royale Belge said on Thursday its share was undervalued and could be worth as much as 10,000 Belgian francs.
"We are still below the intrinsic value of Royale Belge, even if the share has gone up by 2,000 francs this year," chief executive officer Jean-Pierre Gerard told a news conference on 1996 results.

Royale Belge closed up 90 francs at 8,630 on the Brussels bourse ahead of news group current profit rose to 7.1 billion francs in 1996 from 6.2 billion in 1995, in line with analysts' expectations. The share started 1997 at 6,550 francs.

Royale Belge said a mathematical division of its equity of 61.9 billion francs and latent capital gains of 64 billion francs by the number of shares, giving a intrinsic value of around 7,900 francs, did not take into account the full value of its business and reputation.
These intangibles were worth about 2,000 francs more, Gerard said.
